newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open unchanged to $5 lower Monday, in line with weakness overnight in London, traders said.
LIFFE cocoa futures were mainly lower in light trading after a firm start. At the midday break, benchmark September was down two stg at 990 stg a tonne, traded 994 to 987 stg.

New York traders also said strength in the dollar against sterling and other European currencies could pressure CSCE cocoa futures. Overnight, the U.S. currency rose more than a half a cent against the pound and surged to a 7-1/2-year high against the mark.

Friday, New York cocoa futures slumped in lackluster trading. September settled $9 lower at $1,507 a tonne after ranging between $1,516 and $1,504. December fell $10 to $1,556, while the back months sagged $4 to $6.
Technically, traders pegged September's near-term support at $1,496 to $1,494, with stronger support noted at $1,475. Resistance was seen at a chart gap between $1,521 and $1,526.
